one_month_reasoning: One hard event in the window: Q4/FY2026 results and the first formal FY2027 outlook on Tue 2026-10-06 after the close (company release 2026-09-15; not yet reported as of 2026-10-05). The FY26 guide implies Q4 non-GAAP EPS of about $0.77 (FY $2.60 less 9M $1.83), in line with the street, so the stock will trade on the FY27 guide versus the $3.34 consensus (7 analysts, revised up from $2.81 in 30 days) and management's informal ~30% framing. Base rate for this name: the July beat-and-raise (EPS $0.84 vs $0.63) gapped up ~8% then fell ~12% within days, so beats are priced and reactions are large and two-sided. The stock also jumped 11.6% on Oct 2 after Micron's print, which raises the bar. I have no edge on sign, so I keep a lognormal centred on $61.36 with sigma 0.25 (monthly vol ~24% from 83% annual, plus an earnings day), unchanged from round 1.

fair_value.method: Blend of (A) 16.0x NTM EPS at Oct-2027 of ~$3.77 = $60.3 (50%), (B) 17.5x calendar-2027 EPS of $3.47 = $60.7 (25%, 10% below the 19.4x 11-peer CY27 median), and (C) SK hynix's July 2026 purchase price of $62.4 per as-converted share for the SKT preferred (25%); blend $60.9, rounded to $61.

inputs_detail.derivation: Alpha Vantage mean of 7 analysts; replaces the $3.38 I used in round 1, which is management's ~30% framing rather than an independent consensus (stockanalysis FY27 is paywalled)

No FY28 consensus exists, so this is my extrapolation: FY27 $3.34 x 1.12. Growth slows from ~28% to 12% because DRAM contract prices are expected to peak in 2027 with a first decline around Q4 2027 (TrendForce, FutureSearch), which hits Integrated Memory pass-through revenue (57% of Q3 FY26 sales) inside FY28

Inside the peer range (6.6x-31.1x) at about the lower quartile (16.8x), ~18% below the 19.4x 11-peer CY27 median: ~10% persistent discount for memory mix/concentration (see comps_summary) plus ~1.5 turns for applying it one year later to an NTM that by then embeds decelerating, post-peak memory earnings

bear.story: DRAM contract pricing peaks earlier (H1 2027) and rolls over, Integrated Memory revenue and margin reverse, and AI Infrastructure orders are lumpy (one AC customer = 18.2% of sales). NTM EPS at the horizon falls to ~$3.0-3.2 and the market caps it at ~10x (cycle-peak memory multiple, cf. MU 6.6x).

base.story: FY27 guide around the $3.34 consensus is delivered; FY28 grows ~12% as memory pricing plateaus; NTM EPS ~$3.77 at 16x = ~$60-61, i.e. EPS growth offsets multiple compression from 17.7x to 16x.

bull.story: Memory upcycle extends into 2028 and AI Infrastructure scales (neocloud/sovereign wins); FY27 beats toward $3.6 and NTM EPS reaches ~$4.7 at 20x (peer upper half), retesting and passing the $89.86 high.

comps_summary.peer_range: Calendar-2027 P/E (Nasdaq/Zacks fiscal-year consensus month-weighted into CY2027, 2026-10-02 closes; NOT stockanalysis 'Forward PE', which mixes fiscal years): 6.6x (MU) to 31.1x (PLXS), interquartile ~16.8x-22.5x, median 19.4x over 11 names. Excluding MU and the two upper-bound names (NTAP, PLXS) the 8-name systems/EMS core median is 18.45x. Forward EV/EBITDA left null: no consistent forward EBITDA consensus was reachable for PENG or peers, and I would not mix TTM proxies with forward figures.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: PENG trades at 17.7x CY27 EPS of $3.47 (corrected from 16.0x in round 1), ~9% below the 19.4x median and ~4% below the 18.45x core median, i.e. roughly fairly priced, not cheap. I apply 17.5x on CY27 (method B) and 16.0x on horizon NTM EPS (method A), both inside the peer range.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: A ~10% discount, argued as persistent through Oct-2027 rather than a sector call: (1) mix: Integrated Memory was 57% of Q3 FY26 sales ($275.1M of $478.7M, +111% y/y, mostly price) and the DRAM price peak is expected inside the horizon (TrendForce, FutureSearch), and the market already caps near-peak memory earnings (MU 6.6x CY27); this mix cannot change materially in 12 months; (2) concentration: top-10 customers 66% of FY25 sales, one AC customer 18.2% and one IM customer 14.1% (10-K), worse than DELL/HPE/JBL/FLEX; (3) an interim CFO since 2026-07-09 lowers guidance credibility. Against that, PENG's growth (~28% FY27) is above the core median, which is why the discount is limited to ~10% and sits inside the peer range rather than near MU. No premium is argued.

thesis_break_reason: $34 is ~9.8x CY27 EPS of $3.47 and ~13x the FY26 $2.60 base, below every systems/EMS peer (lowest SMCI 9.9x) and near the bear-case value. The stock would get there only on a fundamental earnings reset (FY27 guided or tracking flat on FY26 because DRAM pricing rolls over early, loss of the 18.2% AC customer, or a guide cut), not on ordinary 83%-vol noise. It also sits near the pre-AI re-rating trading range.

reasoning: Round 2 corrections: (a) CY27 = 8/12 FY27 + 4/12 FY28 (my round-1 weights were reversed), and FY27 consensus is $3.34 not $3.38, so CY27 EPS is $3.47 and PENG trades at 17.7x, not 16.0x; (b) I re-pulled Nasdaq/Zacks consensus for every peer myself (one source, one calendarisation rule) and fixed SMCI (9.9x, not 7.5x); with 11 peers the CY27 median is 19.4x (core 8: 18.45x), so PENG is roughly fairly priced versus peers, not cheap; (c) capital structure updated for the July 2026 refinancing (net debt ~$175M principal) and the SK hynix purchase of the preferred at $62.4/as-converted share, which I use as a precedent-transaction leg; (d) government exposure revised to ~0.2% visible. Valuation: 16x horizon NTM EPS of $3.77 = $60.3, 17.5x CY27 = $60.7, transaction $62.4; blended fair value $61 (round 1 $62.3). I extrapolate FY28 at only +12% rather than +20% because the memory price peak is expected inside FY28. Base rates: 83% realized vol after a +127% year and a 32% drawdown from the high; last beat-and-raise sold off 12%; memory-exposed equities usually de-rate ahead of the pricing peak. Distribution: a three-component lognormal mixture on the scenarios (bear $32 p0.25 sigma 0.45, base $61 p0.50 sigma 0.30, bull $94 p0.25 sigma 0.38). Its mean is $62.0, reconciling with the $61 fair value (the $1 gap is the convexity of the bull leg); its median is ~$57 and overall log-sd ~0.54, below realized vol because part of the past year's vol came from the one-off re-rating. That gives P(>=61) 0.44. The 1-month ladder is a neutral sigma-0.25 lognormal around spot because the Oct 6 print is two-sided. Research limits: Alpha Vantage was rate-limited, so the $3.34 consensus is taken from the supervisor-verified pull; JBL has no FY28 consensus on Zacks (assumed +15%); forward EV/EBITDA not available on a consistent basis.
